title: Your capstone batch, honest selling and a 90-day plan

say: Your capstone batch, honest selling, and a 90-day plan.
This is the video for Module 4 of Small-Scale Food Processing.
Your capstone is one real batch, made with everything you have learned. 2 to 5 kg of finished product is enough.
First, fix your recipe and quantities, for example 3 kg of raw groundnuts, 1% salt, in 250 g jars.

say: On day one, open a pack and check appearance, smell, taste and texture. Ask three to five people outside your family to score it out of five.

panel.heading: Sell it, or throw it away?

say: If you see mould, smell anything musty or rancid, find foreign objects, or a CCP failed and could not be corrected, do not sell it or give it away.
Record it as a failed batch, note the cause, and dispose of it. A failed batch with a clear lesson is still good evidence.

panel.heading: Sell it, or throw it away?

say: Vague words like quality and best mean little, because everyone uses them.

panel.heading: Specific facts build trust
items: Not "best quality chips"
Say: fried at a checked temperature
Say: cooled fully, sealed in foil
Confirm payment in your bank app

say: Use specific, truthful facts from your own process. Fried in fresh oil at a checked temperature, cooled fully and sealed in foil pouches to stay crunchy.

say: On WhatsApp, show clear photos, pack size and price. And always confirm payment in your banking app before delivery, because fake transfer alerts are a common scam.

say: In days 1 to 30, make two or three more small batches, changing one thing at a time. Keep full records.

panel.heading: A 90-day plan
items: Days 1 to 30: repeat and refine
Days 31 to 60: test and sell
Days 61 to 90: decide and formalise

say: In days 31 to 60, sell to a small, steady group and track repeat buyers, complaints and yield.
For example, Funmi plans to sell 50 g pouches to 15 regular buyers, with a target of at least 8 repeat buyers.

panel.heading: A 90-day plan
items: Days 1 to 30: repeat and refine
Days 31 to 60: test and sell
Days 61 to 90: decide and formalise

say: In days 61 to 90, review your numbers and decide: continue, change, or move to CAC and NAFDAC registration.
Your product is ready for wider sale when three batches in a row meet your limits, your samples keep, and your price covers full cost.

panel.rule: Ready to sell: three good batches, tested shelf life, a working price.

say: To remember. Plan your batch and record every check as you take it. Never sell a batch with mould, rancidity or a failed CCP. Sell with specific facts. Use batch numbers to trace complaints. And give your 90-day plan real numbers.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Plan, then record checks as you take them
Never sell mould, rancidity or a failed CCP
Sell with specific, truthful facts
Batch numbers turn complaints into fixes
A 90-day plan needs numbers and a decision

say: Now run your capstone batch with stage photos and tasting scores. Prepare your sales kit and complaint routine. Then gather your evidence pack and write your 90-day plan.
Whether you make 2 kg or 200 kg, the same hygiene rules and honesty apply. Continue with the lessons below.
